newsitem.title: USA: W. House to detail reply to medical marijuana laws.
newsitem.headline: W. House to detail reply to medical marijuana laws.

text.p: The Clinton administration, repeating its opposition to the legalisation of drugs, said it will outline on Monday its response to passage of propositions in California and Arizona to allow the medical use of marijuana.

National Drug Control Policy Director Barry McCaffrey, who headed an interagency working group set up to coordinate a broad-based government-wide response, said specific actions would be detailed at a news conference on Monday.
The plan had been reviewed and endorsed by President Bill Clinton, McCaffrey said in a statement released late on Friday.

McCaffrey has been outspoken in his opposition to the propositions passed by voters in the two states last month, warning that the federal government would prosecute doctors who prescribed marijuana under federal laws.

The measures to be announced on Monday were developed to maintain effective enforcement efforts under federal laws; ensure the integrity of the process by which substances are approved as safe and effective; preserve federal drug-free workplace and safety programs; and protect children from increased marijuana availability, McCaffrey said.
He also said the Justice and Health departments would work with Congress to consider changes to federal laws to limit the states' ability to rely on the medical use propositions.

The interagency group would allow continue working with Congres to "re-affirm the national policy of opposing the legalisation of substances that have a high potential for abuse and no accepted medical use."
